correctiveRound.trigger: tester FAIL on acceptance 5 only (.legion/test.json failure): processes.test.ts 'probes a real tmux pane as alive, detects its death, and resurrects it once' Expected "dead" / Received "alive" under LEGION_TMUX_LIVE=1 (CI runs the daemon suite with LEGION_E2E=1 LEGION_TMUX_LIVE=1; a plain bun test skips it).
correctiveRound.rootCauseVerified: Reproduced 1/1 at the tested head before touching anything: the test spawns with project smoke<Date.now()> but the runtime landed on server legion-omp (`tmux -L legion-omp list-windows` afterwards showed `1: legion-42* ... sleep 999`), the test's kill-pane on legion-smoke<...> hit no server, probe stayed alive. processes.test.ts manager()/workerCapFixture built TmuxRuntime with a hardcoded socket "legion-omp"/project "omp"; production index.ts built it from config.project, whereas ProcessManager keys every role token and secret-file name by deps.state.project (pre-branch it derived the tmux socket from deps.state.project too).

fix.production: index.ts: TmuxRuntime gets `socket: legion-${state.project}` and `project: state.project` (was config.project). config.project and state.project agree whenever the state file was created by this config, but ProcessManager reads state.project everywhere (paneSecretFiles names, liveSecretFiles prune, role tokens), so the runtime's server and secret-file names must come from the same value — byte-identical to the pre-branch derivation. Said so per the corrective instructions.
fix.tests: processes.test.ts manager(): socket/project derived from the fixture's state.project (comment explains why); processes.thermo-ops.test.ts helper: same derivation; 'creates the first live root without a default bash window' now asserts `windows.exitCode === 0` and that the listing contains legion-42 before asserting no bash window, so a spawn onto another server can no longer pass it vacuously.
